channel.title: Fluxa Direct Updates
channel.description: Stable updates for Fluxa Direct on Apple silicon.

item.description:
Fluxa 2.9.1

This update asks for your permissions one last time. Until now every Fluxa build was signed with a throwaway identity that changed on each release, so macOS treated each update as an unknown app and asked again for keychain and Accessibility access. Fluxa is now signed with a stable identity, so after granting them once more they will persist across all future updates.

  • Antigravity usage now works. The previous release read Google's Cloud Code API, which refuses individual free-tier accounts; quota is now read from the helper process Antigravity already runs on this Mac. Fluxa reads no credential, stores no token, and the request never leaves your machine. The meters appear only while Antigravity is open.
  • Rate limits are handled properly. When a provider asks Fluxa to back off, it now says when the meters return instead of showing a bare HTTP error, and stops re-requesting until then.

Requires macOS 14 or later and Apple silicon. Preferences, action order and history are unchanged by this update.

Fluxa is signed with a self-signed certificate and is not notarized, so first launch after a fresh download still needs the usual right-click > Open.

Fluxa 2.8.0

  • Battery and power: charge percentage and time-remaining metrics for the internal battery, plus AC/battery power source. Time remaining is debounced against jumpy IOKit estimates before it's shown.
  • Peripheral battery: Magic Mouse/Keyboard/Trackpad battery levels shown in the System Dashboard, with presence hysteresis so a sleeping device doesn't flicker in and out of the list.
  • Threshold alerts: optional notifications when CPU, die temperature or free disk space cross a limit, with dwell time and hysteresis so a brief spike doesn't spam notifications. Off by default; enable per-metric in Customize > System.

Requires macOS 14 or later and Apple silicon. Preferences, action order and history are unchanged by this update.

Fluxa is ad-hoc signed, not notarized. A changed signing identity may require renewed macOS permissions.

## Fluxa 2.7.1
- New **Clean URL** quick action: strips tracking parameters (`utm_*`, `fbclid`, `gclid`, and more) from the clipboard's URL, with host-specific rules for YouTube, Amazon and X. - The system dashboard now reads disk (used percentage, free space, read/write throughput) and network (combined download/upload) alongside CPU, GPU, memory and temperature.
This supersedes 2.7.0 (14), which was never a valid update target: a local build had already claimed build number 14 on the developer's Mac before that release was cut, so Sparkle's build-number comparison could never offer it. No functional code changed since 2.7.0.
Requires macOS 14 or later and Apple silicon. Preferences, action order and history are unchanged by this update.
Fluxa is ad-hoc signed, not notarized. A changed signing identity may require renewed macOS permissions.

Fluxa 2.6.2

  • Customize is grouped into General, Actions, System, Agents and Updates tabs. The panel widens for Customize and About and still transitions in place, without a separate settings window.
  • About fits version and build, the public GitHub card, Check for Updates and the optional support link into one screen.
  • The Agent Usage window sizes itself to its content, showing both quota cards and the complete daily contribution grids without an inner scrollbar.

Requires macOS 14 or later and Apple silicon. Preferences, action order and history are unchanged by this update.

Fluxa is ad-hoc signed, not notarized. A changed signing identity may require renewed macOS permissions.

Fluxa 2.6.1

  • Sparkle updates from About, with optional automatic checks in Customize. Download and installation require confirmation.
  • Optional Permissions & First Run setup for Accessibility, Automation, Bluetooth and Claude credential access.
  • Branded installer with an English first-launch guide.

Requires macOS 14 or later and Apple silicon. Users of v2.5.0 and earlier must install this first updater-enabled release manually once.

Fluxa is ad-hoc signed, not notarized. A changed signing identity may require renewed macOS permissions.
